title: Migrating to AWS: CAF, adoption strategies and migration resources
learningObjective: Describe the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework perspectives and outcomes, cloud adoption and migration strategies, and the resources that support migration.
foundation: The AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF) organises guidance into six perspectives so an organisation can plan its move to the cloud: Business, People, Governance, Platform, Security and Operations.
Migration strategies (the '7 Rs') describe what to do with each application: rehost, replatform, refactor, repurchase, retire, retain or relocate.
AWS provides tools, programs and partners to help, such as AWS Migration Hub, Application Migration Service, DMS and Migration Evaluator.
engineer: CAF business outcomes: reduced business risk, improved ESG (environmental, social and governance) performance, increased revenue and increased operational efficiency. Transformation domains: technology, process, organisation, product.

Perspectives: Business (strategy, portfolio, innovation), People (culture, workforce, change), Governance (program/portfolio, risk, cloud financial management), Platform (architecture, engineering, CI/CD), Security (identity, detection, data protection, incident response), Operations (observability, incident and problem management).

7 Rs: Rehost (lift and shift, often with AWS Application Migration Service), Replatform (for example to Amazon RDS), Refactor/re-architect (cloud-native), Repurchase (move to SaaS), Retire, Retain, Relocate (for example VMware Cloud on AWS).

Migration resources: AWS Migration Hub (track migrations), AWS Application Discovery Service and Migration Evaluator (discovery and business case), AWS Application Migration Service (rehost servers), AWS DMS with SCT (database migration including ongoing replication), AWS Snow Family and DataSync (data transfer), AWS Prescriptive Guidance, AWS Professional Services and partners, and the Migration Acceleration Program (MAP).

example.title: A data center exit
body: A company must leave its data center in a year. Migration Evaluator builds the business case, Application Migration Service rehosts 300 VMs, DMS replicates the Oracle databases to Aurora with minimal downtime (SCT converts schemas), and old reporting apps are retired.

prerequisites: An AWS account (use an IAM Identity Center user, not root)
permissions: Read-only access to explore; least-privilege permissions to change resources
limits: Conceptual objective: explore in the console; no configuration limits are tested
portal: AWS Migration Hub > Discover / Assess / Migrate.
AWS DMS > Create replication instance and task.

walkthrough.subtitle: Move one company's data center to AWS: plan with the CAF, choose a strategy per app, use the right tools.
learn: Cloud adoption: the AWS CAF and its business outcomes
Migration tools and help (including database replication)

steps.label: Where to start?
steps.title: 200 applications and a lease that ends next year
body: A company must leave its data center. Some apps are old, some are critical, some nobody uses.
Moving them all the same way would be slow and risky. It needs a plan, a strategy for each app, and tools.

steps.label: AWS CAF
steps.title: Plan with the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework
body: The AWS CAF is AWS's guidance for organising a cloud transformation. It is not only about technology.
It names four business outcomes the move should bring: reduced business risk, improved ESG (environmental, social and governance) performance, increased revenue, and increased operational efficiency.

steps.label: Perspectives
steps.title: Six perspectives: everyone has a part
body: Business, People and Governance are the business side: strategy, skills and culture, and risk and cloud financial management.
Platform, Security and Operations are the technical side: architecture, protection, and running things day to day.

callout.text: Exam tip: People = training and culture; Governance = cost and risk control; Platform = architecture.

steps.label: 7 Rs
steps.title: Choose a strategy per app: the 7 Rs
body: Rehost (lift and shift as-is). Replatform (small changes, for example move the database to Amazon RDS). Refactor (re-architect to be cloud-native). Repurchase (switch to SaaS).
Retire (switch it off). Retain (keep it on-premises for now). Relocate (move VMware workloads as they are).

steps.label: Tools
steps.title: Use the right migration tools
body: AWS Application Migration Service copies servers to AWS for rehosting with minimal downtime.

AWS Database Migration Service (DMS) moves databases while the source keeps running, using continuous replication. The Schema Conversion Tool (SCT) converts the schema when the engine changes, for example Oracle to Aurora PostgreSQL.

callout.text: Database replication lets the old database keep serving users until you switch over. That is how you cut downtime.

steps.label: The plan
steps.title: Case: three apps, three strategies
body: The old HR app: retire it, because nobody uses it. The shop: rehost now with Application Migration Service, refactor later. The billing database: replatform to RDS with DMS replication, then switch over on a quiet night.
AWS Prescriptive Guidance, AWS Professional Services and AWS Partners help plan and run the work.

steps.label: Recap
steps.title: Plan, choose, move
body: A migration is a business change, a strategy per app, and the right tools.
recap: CAF outcomes: less risk, better ESG, more revenue, more efficiency
Six perspectives: Business, People, Governance, Platform, Security, Operations
7 Rs: rehost, replatform, refactor, repurchase, retire, retain, relocate
Application Migration Service rehosts servers; DMS + SCT move databases with replication
Prescriptive Guidance, Professional Services and Partners help
